academic_source: P001 (Gao, Han, Li & Zhou 2018, Market Intraday Momentum, JFE)
specification: sign(first 30-min bar return) predicts direction traded in the last 30-min bar of the same session; original spec, no filters/modifications (section 11A)
sample_period: 2026-06-08 to 2026-09-11 (~95 calendar days, 67 trading days with data)
important_caveat: THIS IS NOT A VALID ACADEMIC REPLICATION OR A STATISTICALLY MEANINGFUL BACKTEST. It is a pipeline smoke test on the only data this environment's IBKR connector can reach (see data/metadata/depth_assessment.json) -- 67 trades is far below the mandate's own 100+ independent trades minimum (section 24) and the naive t-stats below are NOT HAC/Newey-West adjusted (section 45). No conclusion about whether the Gao et al. effect is real should be drawn from this run. It exists to prove entry/exit/cost-model mechanics are correct end-to-end, and it happens to also be the first real (if statistically weak) look at this specification on live MES data.
conclusion: Net P&L is negative in all three cost scenarios, and GROSS P&L (before any commission/fee/spread/slippage) is also negative (-$158.75 base window), so this is not simply a costs problem: the original sign(first-half-hour) -> last-half-hour direction did not work in this specific ~3-month window. Per section 21 ('too few independent observations') and section 93 ('failure is a valid output'), this does not currently qualify as a working strategy -- but 67 trades in one regime is also nowhere near enough to conclude the effect is dead. Status: provisionally not passing; genuinely undecided pending real multi-year data.
